turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have been thinking about how to make social plans feel a bit easier while I am getting used to my appetite being different. I don't want every invitation to turn into a discussion about the injection, and I don't want to spend the whole time explaining myself when other people are just enjoying their evening. I know I can make choices for myself, but I sometimes get stuck because I think about the conversation around the food before I think about the food itself. Could I ask for some general suggestions for situations where I am eating with other people and don't want it to feel complicated?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Hi Kai, I can help with general eating tips. What kind of meal or situation are you thinking about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The part I meant to mention is restaurants. I was concentrating on the social side and forgot to say where we would actually be eating. I would like some ideas for looking at a menu without feeling as if I need to finish the largest main meal just because that is what everyone else orders. I am not trying to avoid going out or to turn the evening into a strict food exercise. I want to enjoy the meal and have a portion that feels comfortable, but I don't know what simple choices to look for when there are lots of things on the menu.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Smaller portions are a useful place to start. You could choose an entrée-sized meal, share a dish if you want to, or set some aside. Eat at a comfortable pace and choose something you enjoy; you don't need to match someone else's portion.
